title: A Founder's unilateral power over Omni Documents ends permanently at the Transformation Primitive
content:
A.1.14.2.8 and A.1.14.2.8.1 grant a startup-phase exception: "Prior to the Invocation and codification of the Prime Transformation or Executor Transformation Primitive within an Agent Artifact, the Agent's Founder may unilaterally create new Omni Documents or edit existing Omni Documents."

A.1.14.2.8.2 closes it at a defined event: after that invocation the Founder "no longer has the discretion to unilaterally create new Omni Documents or edit existing Omni Documents. Instead, the Agent Artifact can only be updated or changed through existing Omni Documents or the governance process defined in the Root Edit Primitive."

The reasoning is that governance requires a governed population. Before Transformation there is no meaningful token holder body to vote, so insisting on the Root Edit process would make bootstrapping impossible — and a chicken-and-egg problem in the amendment process would block the Agent from ever writing the rules by which it is amended.

What makes this safe is that the sunset is tied to a discrete, publicly observable state change rather than to a date, a milestone judgment, or the Founder's own discretion. The Founder cannot extend their own window, and the transition is binary.

The residual risk is that Founder-era Omni Documents survive the transition with full force. Whatever the Founder wrote unilaterally becomes the deterministic logic that Executors will execute without a vote — so the real exercise of founder power is not the temporary editing right but the permanent content it leaves behind, changeable thereafter only by the token holders it created.
description: Before the Prime or Executor Transformation Primitive is invoked and codified, the Founder may create and edit Omni Documents alone;
